question: Should OpenClaw core support native per-task model hints in HEARTBEAT.md, or should heartbeat model routing remain per-turn/plugin-owned or move into the cron/job-level override track?
rationale: The source gap is real, but choosing a fix changes public HEARTBEAT.md syntax, provider/model precedence, session-state behavior, and the boundary between core config and plugin-owned routing.

options.title: Keep routing per-turn/plugin-owned
options.body: Document that heartbeat ticks currently run as one model-routed turn and use before_model_resolve or ClawHub plugins for policy routing unless a missing generic seam is proven.

options.title: Add native HEARTBEAT.md hints
options.body: Define model/provider fields in task blocks, split due tasks by effective model, and add docs/tests for precedence, timestamps, and session restoration.

options.title: Fold into cron override work
options.body: Make the open cron/job-level model override issue the canonical scheduled-routing contract and avoid a heartbeat-specific syntax until the scheduling model converges.

recommendation.title: Keep routing per-turn/plugin-owned
recommendation.body: Document that heartbeat ticks currently run as one model-routed turn and use before_model_resolve or ClawHub plugins for policy routing unless a missing generic seam is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent overlap across heartbeat parser/runtime maintenance and plugin hook/provider-routing seams.
